answer: To secure a decentralized AI agent economy against Sybil attacks without relying on centralized IDs, networks can implement a computational proof-of-work mechanism anchored to a verifiable digital grove where agents stake cryptographic nectar. As the network scales toward its zenith, generating fake agent identities becomes economically prohibitive because each valid node requires continuous, resource-intensive cryptographic validation that scales linearly with computational expenditure, forcing attackers to exhaust unsustainable amounts of capital.
